newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Duma proposes to change insurance law.
newsitem.headline: Russia Duma proposes to change insurance law.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament budget committee on Monday proposed an increase in insurers' minimum authorised capital and a requirement on Russian companies and individuals to use local insurers for property insurance.
A document, obtained by Reuters, proposes raising insurers' minimum authorised capital to about 2.09 billion roubles for companies involved in non-life insurance.

It proposes raising minimum authorised capital of companies, which provide life-insurance to about 2.92 billion roubles. It proposes raising the minimum authorised capital for companies involved solely in re-insurance to 4.17 billion roubles.
At present the minimum required authorised capital for Russian insurers is two million roubles.

The document proposes limiting Russian companies and individuals to insuring their property only with Russian insurers. The only exclusion is insurance of civil responsibility of car-owners travelling abroad, it said.
Russia's ailing insurance market raised 27.4 trillion roubles in premiums in 1996, a rise of 4.3 percent over 1995 but a fall in real terms given 1996 annual inflation of 22 percent.

Both the government and insurers fear 1999 when a ban on foreign insurance companies' activity in Russia expires. They all call for a curb in foreigners' participation on the Russian insurance market.
